problem.paragraph: What is the relationship between the point $$\left( {4,7} \right)$$ and the vector $$\langle{4,7}\rangle$$ ? Illustrate with a sketch.
Name all the equal vectors in the parallelogram shown.

image.alt: Details Eighth vectors, arranged in the form of a parallelogram and its diagonals, are displayed. The first vector begins from D, and runs horizontally rightward until C. The second vector begins at C, slopes steeply upward to the right and ends at B. The third vector begins at D, and slopes steeply upward to the left, parallel to the second vector until a point A. From A, the fourth vector runs horizontally rightward until it reaches B, thus completing a parallelogram A B C D with side A B on top. From D, the fifth vector slopes upward to the right until D. From C, the sixth vector slopes upward to the left to reach A, crossing the fifth vector at E. D B and C A form the diagonals of the parallelogram. From D, the seventh vector runs along the diagonal D B until E. From C, the eighth vector runs along with the diagonal C A until E.

Corner Reflectors Suppose the three coordinate planes are all mirrored, forming a corner reflector, and a light ray given by the vector $$\mathbf{a} = {\langle{a_{1},a_{2},a_{3}}\rangle}$$ first strikes the $$\mathit{xz}$$ -plane, as shown in the figure. Use the fact that the angle of incidence equals the angle of reflection to show that the direction of the reflected ray is given by $$\mathbf{b} = {\langle{a_{1}, - a_{2},a_{3}}\rangle}$$ . Deduce that, after being reflected by all three mutually perpendicular mirrors, the resulting ray is parallel to the initial ray. (Scientists have used this principle, together with laser beams and an array of corner reflectors on the moon, to calculate very precisely the distance from Earth to the moon.)

image.alt: Details A ray is graphed in the first octant of the x y z coordinate space. The positive x axis slopes down and to the left. The positive y axis slopes slightly down and to the right. The positive z axis runs vertically upward. The ray enters from the bottom left, meets the x z plane, and then slopes downward to the right, meets the x y plane, slopes upward to the right, meets the y z plane, slopes downward to the right, and exits at the bottom.

exercises.paragraph: Josiah Willard Gibbs (1839–1903), a professor of mathematical physics at Yale College, published the first book on vectors, Vector Analysis, in 1881. More complicated objects, called quaternions, had earlier been invented by Sir William Rowan Hamilton as mathematical tools for describing space, but they weren’t easy for scientists to use. Quaternions have a scalar part and a vector part. Gibb’s idea was to use the vector part separately. Maxwell and Heaviside had similar ideas, but Gibb’s approach has proved to be the most convenient way to study space.
